comments.mergedPostDetails: Sometimes, you make a mistake during T-pose calibration, and your FBT calibration is a bit off. Or the avatar may enter T-pose in an inconvenient location, such as partially clipping into an object, making it hard to align with the avatar. It would be very convenient if there was a faster way to re-enter T-pose to fix up calibration than switching into another avatar and back.

comments.value:
@{5a6ffbd6337de65dbe2d92a1|full_name}: 

I appreciate the notes but because you directed them at me I will respond with this,

- yes I use playspace mover, now why should I use a third party workaround to something that can easily be fixed be spawning the avatar correctly at the hmd position. I dont have this issue, but its good to know the workaround I guess. Also this is a bad idea as it could mess up the calibration height if the playspace is not moved properly

- whats so hard about this? its most likely attaching the trackers as an IK follow point, not that hard to store the information as they are already doing it anyway. You can switch to a non-humanoid avatar then back to your previous humanoid and all the calibration will still be there. In addition as long as you dont calibrate on a new avatar you can switch back and the calibration will still be there. They just need to store it externally per avatar id in a file or whatever solution they choose.

- I have already done the temporary neck fix. As far as im aware vrchat is aware of the full body IK issues and should be getting a fix out because the neck weight painting does not fix the view point not staying in the head. Its already been mentioned that the head is not 100% weighted to the viewpoint IK which is one of the causes for this issue and something we cant fix with just the neck workaround. The neck fix also makes the bends look horrendous

comments.value:
@{5ab3ad272b67505f726c2a8f|full_name}: 
As far as I know after you reduce the neck bone size and merge its weights to the head you don't need to remove the neck vertex group. Do note removing the neck vertex group causes the latest vrcsdk to throw error (no neck bone).
Refering the this image I uploaded you can see the neck is really small, while the head is much larger. You then estimate how far the eyes are realitive to the head bone, for this case the head bone isn't big enough and won't be able to see over the breasts. So you'd want to make the head bone taller and perhaps move the head and neck bone down - it takes a few tries per model before you can get it perfect.
When you are lying down the fullbody ik is trash, you'd honestly want to move the eyes OR head and neck bone further out from the model. I don't bother too much with female models with large beasts since it's painful to get it right, better to just make two model versions - one for lying down and one for standing.
I can't believe this feature doesn't exist yet =/

details:
Full Body Tracking requires some trail and error to get just right. It's annoying to switch to another avatar and the having to apply the full-body tracking to that one before you are able to recalibrate the feature to the avatar you want it to be. 

A way to recalibrate the tracking on an avatar you are using right now would be very helpful when troubleshooting different skeleton proportions.
title: Recalibrate button on already-in-use avatars for full-body tracking
